cases.question: List all departments with their ID and name ordered by department name ascending.
cases.notes: Basic projection and sorting on the departments table.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT department_id, department_name FROM departments ORDER BY department_name ASC;

cases.question: Find all courses that offer exactly 4 credits ordered by course ID.
cases.notes: Exact integer equality filtering on credits.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT course_id, course_name, credits FROM courses WHERE credits = 4 ORDER BY course_id ASC;

cases.question: List all students enrolled in the academic year 2023 ordered by student ID.
cases.notes: Cohort filtering on student enrollment year.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT student_id, student_name, enrollment_year FROM students WHERE enrollment_year = 2023 ORDER BY student_id ASC;

cases.question: Show all courses offering 3 credits ordered by course name ascending.
cases.notes: Integer filtering combined with text alphabetical sorting.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT course_id, course_name, credits FROM courses WHERE credits = 3 ORDER BY course_name ASC;

cases.question: What is the total number of students in the university?
cases.notes: Scalar count aggregation on students table.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_students FROM students;

cases.question: What is the average marks scored across all enrollments?
cases.notes: Scalar floating-point average aggregation on marks.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(marks), 2) AS average_marks FROM enrollments;

cases.question: What are the lowest and highest marks scored by any student?
cases.notes: Dual scalar boundary aggregations (MIN and MAX).
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT MIN(marks) AS min_marks, MAX(marks) AS max_marks FROM enrollments;

cases.question: What is the total sum of credit hours offered across all courses?
cases.notes: Sum aggregation on integer course credits.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT SUM(credits) AS total_credits FROM courses;

cases.question: How many students are there in each department? Show department name and student count ordered by student count descending.
cases.notes: Categorical count grouping with outer join and secondary ordering.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT d.department_name, COUNT(s.student_id) AS student_count FROM departments d LEFT JOIN students s ON d.department_id = s.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name ORDER BY student_count DESC, d.department_name ASC;

cases.question: Calculate the average marks for each course and list course name and average marks ordered by average marks descending.
cases.notes: Grouped average marks per course.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT c.course_name, ROUND(AVG(e.marks), 2) AS avg_marks FROM courses c JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name ORDER BY avg_marks DESC, c.course_name ASC;

cases.question: Count the number of courses offered by each department ordered by course count descending.
cases.notes: Outer join grouping ensuring departments with 0 courses are preserved.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT d.department_name, COUNT(c.course_id) AS course_count FROM departments d LEFT JOIN courses c ON d.department_id = c.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name ORDER BY course_count DESC, d.department_name ASC;

cases.question: Show the number of course enrollments in each semester ordered by semester.
cases.notes: Single-table aggregation grouped by semester.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT semester, COUNT(*) AS enrollment_count FROM enrollments GROUP BY semester ORDER BY semester ASC;

cases.question: List each student's ID, name, and their department name ordered by student ID.
cases.notes: Two-table inner join on department_id.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, d.department_name FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.department_id = d.department_id ORDER BY s.student_id ASC;

cases.question: List all courses and the students enrolled in them, showing course name and student name ordered by course name and student name.
cases.notes: Three-table relational join linking courses and students through enrollments.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT c.course_name, s.student_name FROM enrollments e JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.course_id JOIN students s ON e.student_id = s.student_id ORDER BY c.course_name ASC, s.student_name ASC;

cases.question: Show course name, department name, and credits for all courses ordered by course name.
cases.notes: Two-table inner join between courses and departments.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT c.course_name, d.department_name, c.credits FROM courses c JOIN departments d ON c.department_id = d.department_id ORDER BY c.course_name ASC;

cases.question: List the names and marks of all students enrolled in Introduction to Programming ordered by marks descending.
cases.notes: Three-table join with literal string equality filter on course_name.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT s.student_name, e.marks FROM enrollments e JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.course_id JOIN students s ON e.student_id = s.student_id WHERE c.course_name = 'Introduction to Programming' ORDER BY e.marks DESC, s.student_name ASC;

cases.question: Find all students who have scored higher than the overall average marks across all enrollments. Show student name and marks ordered by marks descending.
cases.notes: Subquery filter comparing individual row marks against scalar aggregate average.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT DISTINCT s.student_name, e.marks FROM enrollments e JOIN students s ON e.student_id = s.student_id WHERE e.marks > (SELECT AVG(marks) FROM enrollments) ORDER BY e.marks DESC, s.student_name ASC;

cases.question: Which courses currently have zero student enrollments? Show course ID and course name.
cases.notes: Anti-join pattern using LEFT JOIN and IS NULL check on foreign key.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id WHERE e.enrollment_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.course_id ASC;

cases.question: Identify the top 3 students with the highest average marks across their courses. Show student name and average marks rounded to 2 decimals.
cases.notes: Grouped aggregate with TOP-3 limit and tie-break ordering.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT s.student_name, ROUND(AVG(e.marks), 2) AS avg_marks FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name ORDER BY avg_marks DESC, s.student_name ASC LIMIT 3;

cases.question: Which department has the most students enrolled? Return the department name and count.
cases.notes: Aggregated maximum group with LIMIT 1.
cases.candidate_sql: SELECT d.department_name, COUNT(s.student_id) AS total_students FROM departments d JOIN students s ON d.department_id = s.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name ORDER BY total_students DESC, d.department_name ASC LIMIT 1;
